headline: Foreign investors sold a huge ₹12,944 crore of Indian shares yesterday and Nifty fell 1.6% to a 52-week low. Oil above $104 and very high US bond rates are the main reasons, but Indian funds bought almost as much as foreigners sold.

mood.label: Negative
mood.why: The dashboard's score is −34 (bearish), but only 2 of its 4 direction checks agree, so the signal is weak.

key_points.text: The data shows Nifty closed at **22,232**, down 1.6%, below all three of its average lines, and it touched a 52-week low of 22,180 during the day.
FIIs (foreign investors) sold **₹12,944 crore** in cash shares, almost three times their recent daily average. Their bets in index futures are only 8.5% on a rise.
DIIs (Indian funds like mutual funds) bought **₹10,703 crore**, soaking up about 83% of the foreign selling. This is why the fall was not worse.
Brent crude rose 3.8% to **$104** a barrel on Middle East shipping attacks. India buys most of its oil abroad, so this raises costs, inflation and pressure on the rupee.
GIFT Nifty (an early indicator traded overnight) was near **22,370**, about 80 points up, as oil eased a little in Asian trade. A small bounce at the open is possible, but the trend is still down.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend is clearly down, but the dashboard's checks don't fully agree, so confidence is low.

points.text: Nifty is below its 20-day (23,018), 50-day (23,761) and 200-day (24,283) averages, and recent highs and lows keep getting lower. The trend check scores the lowest possible, **−2**.
In futures, the price fell 1.6% while the number of open contracts rose 1.2%. My read: traders opened **new bets on a fall**, not just closed old bets on a rise.

The option-chain check scores **+1.3** (bullish). It reads the big jump in call contracts at 22,300–22,500 as buying, since their option prices rose. On a 1.6% down day this is unusual, so I would not lean on it much.
The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) is **0.73**, close to 0.70, the level the dashboard treats as too much fear. Below that, its model would flip to expecting a bounce.
India VIX (the fear gauge) jumped about 10% to **15.3**, higher than 74% of the past year. Expect bigger daily swings than usual.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreigners are selling hard and Indian funds are buying almost as hard. That tug-of-war decides the next move.

points.text: FIIs have now sold for 3 days in a row in the dashboard's data, **₹22,026 crore** so far in October. Reports say it is their ninth straight selling day.
DIIs bought ₹10,703 crore yesterday and **₹20,389 crore** this month. Steady Indian buying is the main support under the market.

Only **8.5%** of FII index-futures positions bet on a rise, down from 9.2%. Below 10% has sometimes come before sharp rebounds, when they rush to close bets on a fall, but there is no sign of that yet.
FIIs added a lot of index put options (insurance against a fall), up about **91,000** contracts net. They are protecting against more downside.
The latest NSDL data (16–30 Sept) shows FIIs sold most in banks and finance (**₹6,943 crore**), then oil and gas, then autos.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Costly oil, very high US bond rates and a strong dollar are all pulling money away from India.

points.text: Brent crude is **$104**, up 37% in 3 months. Reuters linked the latest jump to attacks on ships in the Gulf. Early Friday it eased about 0.8% to around $103.
The US 10-year bond rate is **5.24%**, up 0.40 points in a month and near its highest since 2002. Safe US bonds paying this much pull foreign money out of shares like India's.
The rupee is at **96.79** per dollar, its weakest level of the past year, and the dollar index is up 3.4% in a month. A weak rupee cuts foreign investors' returns.
The RBI raised its main lending rate by 0.25% to **5.50%** on 7 October, its first rise in nearly four years, and said cuts are off the table. Costlier loans hurt banks, autos and property shares.
US shares slipped: S&P 500 down 0.5%, Nasdaq down **1.25%** on worries about AI companies. The dashboard flags that US bond markets expect the Fed to raise rates, which would be bad for India.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: TCS kicked off the results season with steady but not exciting numbers.

points.text: TCS revenue grew 11.2% and profit **14.9%** vs last year. The dashboard rates this "In line", since profit grew less than 20%.
Compared with the last quarter, TCS revenue grew only **1.3%**, and one report says profit came in slightly below analyst estimates.
TCS declared a **₹12** dividend and plans to buy MHP for ₹3,484 crore. A weak rupee helps IT exporters, which may cushion IT shares.
One report says IT shares are in focus today due to a new **US visa suspension** affecting Indian IT firms. I couldn't confirm the details from a second source.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: Inflation data, big bank results and oil prices over the next two weeks will decide whether this fall continues.

points.text: India's inflation figure comes on **12 October** at 4 pm. A high number would back more RBI rate rises; a soft one would ease worries.
HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank report on **17 October**. Banks are Nifty's biggest weight and the sector FIIs sold most.
The US Fed decides on rates around midnight IST on **29 October**. A rise would likely push more foreign money out.
What would prove the bearish read wrong: oil falling back below $100, FII selling slowing, and FII futures bets on a rise climbing back **above 10%**.

levels.note: A close above 22,700 would mean call sellers have given up and a bounce is gaining strength; a close below 22,000 would break the biggest put wall and open room for a deeper fall.

watch.text: The open. GIFT Nifty points to a small gain; see if it holds or gets sold into, as in recent days.
Brent crude near $103–104. Any new Middle East attacks could push it higher and hurt Indian shares.
Today's FII and DII figures, out after the close. Watch if Indian funds keep absorbing the selling.
US consumer mood and inflation expectations survey. Higher inflation expectations would keep US bond rates high.
IT shares, after TCS results and the US visa report.

bottom_line: The dashboard reads the market as bearish (score −34), driven by a clear downtrend and fresh bets on a fall in futures, but only 2 of its 4 checks agree, so confidence is low. The outside world backs the bearish side: oil above $100, US bond rates near 24-year highs, the weakest rupee in a year and an RBI that has started raising rates. The main risk to this read is a sharp rebound: FIIs are extremely one-sided with only 8.5% of their futures bets on a rise, fear is high, and Indian funds are buying heavily. A small bounce today would not change the trend unless Nifty gets back above 22,700.
